Infrastructure and scaling.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
Office 365 Core Engineer.
Infrastructure and scaling.

positions.title: Graduate Research Assistant
positions.description:
I work with the E-Crime Investigative Technologies and work on the following:
• GPU based distributed cracking system. The goal of this project is to aid Law Enforcement agencies to unencrypt
incriminatory evidence. I guided my team by aiming to deploy using Docker.
• Machine Learning Driven Mobile Forensics. Project funded by the National Institute of Justice. I worked with the
iOS team to extract artifacts without compromising the forensic validity of the evidence.
• I contributed with scripts for “I Know What You Did Last Summer: Your Smart Home Internet of Things and Your
iPhone Forensically Ratting You Out” which will be published in ARES 2018.

positions.title: Graduate Teaching Assistant
positions.description: Grader and Assistant for the courses “Computer Fluency” and “Programming I”.

projects.title: Distributed Cracking System
projects.description: Along another master’s student we are developing a system to perform password cracking in a distributed environment. We are using docker and docker swarm to deploy the different services. I am currently working on the web server, which uses Ruby on Rails and a PostgreSQL database. I am guiding my teammate with the development of the distributed system using Python and Django. My main contribution to this project was the design of the database structure and the general architecture of the project.

projects.title: Targeted Data Extraction System for Mobile Devices
projects.description: This project was developed thanks to a grant obtained from the National Institute of Justice. The main goal of it is to acquire evidence from mobile devices without investigators having to look at witnesses’ personal or sensitive information. I worked on the iOS forensic analysis and application development. My duties were to transfer information between a workstation and the mobile device in a sound forensic way. I also inspected and retrieved information from the off-device backup. Finally, I had the task to fix general bugs.
